title: Entitlement Navigator: permission-ripple simulator & microflow canvas for workspace RBAC
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Design a compact, single-panel Entitlement Navigator that surfaces who has access, why they have it (role inheritance/policy), and what changes ripple across resources when a permission is modified. The feature targets workspace admins and security reviewers who need rapid triage and impact estimation without leaving the Console.

Scope: 1) Permission-ripple simulator: lightweight control to toggle a role/permission and preview affected resources and users. 2) Microflow canvas: condensed activity stream showing the last 90 days of grants, expirations, and delegated approvals. 3) Compact policy snapshot: human-readable breakdown of role composition and external group mappings.

Success metrics: reduce time-to-incident-triage by 30% (from internal baseline), increase completion rate of ad-hoc access reviews in-console by 25%, and get >80% usability score from admin participants in prototype testing.

Non-goals: full audit replay session (separate workstream), deep forensics across cross-workspace grants, or replacing the full Access Workbench UX. This is a targeted lightweight tool for quick decisions and rollbacks.
mockups: Figma: Compact panel with header, search, ripple-simulator toggle, microflow canvas lane, policy snapshot accordion
Prototype: interactive toggles showing live counts and escape hatch to 'preview rollback' link
comments: 2026-02-14 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial ticket created after kickoff with PM and infra. Captured scope and success metrics. Reference PRD linked. Asked ENG for feasibility note on computing ripple effects in <200ms for 10k user/role graphs.

2026-02-18 - Maya Chen: Low-fidelity wires uploaded to Figma. Iteration focused on single-panel flow to avoid modal-jump fatigue. Decided to prioritize a simulated preview (no writes) for initial release to avoid backend permission-change hazards.

2026-02-23 - Rafael Gomez (engineering comment): Feasibility OK with precomputed denormalized role graph and lightweight cache. Major trade-off: real-time accuracy vs latency; proposal to run a 'fast stale-tolerant' snapshot with TTL 30s and background exact consistency job.

2026-02-28 - PM (Lena Ortiz): Requested 'quick revoke preview' CTA be clearly labeled and gated behind a confirmation flow. Also asked for telemetry hooks: preview_opened, ripple_estimated_count, preview_confirmed.

2026-03-03 - Accessibility review (Sofia Patel): Color contrast for ripple heat overlays must be >=4.5:1; recommend pattern alternatives (dot badges + text) for colorblind users. Keyboard flow acceptable but needs ARIA live regions for simulation results.

2026-03-06 - Usability test round 1 (5 admins): Key findings - users liked the quick impact numbers but were confused by 'inherited via group' label. Action: add a microcopy tooltip explaining inheritance paths and an example short-hand ("Role X via Group Y").

2026-03-09 - Design review session notes: PM, Eng, Security present. Agreement: phase 1 = read-only simulator + microflow canvas + export CSV. Phase 2 = controlled rollouts (canary revocations) and audit playbacks. Security asked for audit log linkability from each event in microflow.

2026-03-12 - Maya Chen: Updated hi-fi prototype with compact policy snapshot accordion, explicit inbound/external grant badges, and 'preview rollback' disabled by default. Pushed updated specs to Confluence and requested ENG spike for snapshot TTL behavior. Ready for design handoff.

2026-03-12 - Next steps: ENG spike (ENG-41233) to land by 2026-03-17; PM to schedule beta with two enterprise customers; accessibility follow-up to include screen-reader walkthroughs; design handoff to begin after spike results.
review_feedback: PM: make telemetry explicit and map to billing/event schema
Eng: prefer eventual-consistent snapshot with fast-approximation for initial preview
Security: require per-event linkable audit entry and ensure preview does not expose hidden system roles
Design: simplify microflow timeline to 3 lanes (grants, expirations, escalations) to reduce visual noise
